senses: Affected by leucism.
ety: From leucism + -istic, ultimately from Latinized form of Ancient Greek λευκός (leukós, “white”).

senses: Somewhat long.
examples: She had a longish face scribbled all over with wrinkles.
It was a longish time before I received a reply to my letter.

senses: A small local restaurant in (usually rural) Italy.
ety: Borrowed from Italian osteria. Doublet of hostry.

senses: Any of several thermoplastic materials made from polyacrylates.
A fibre made from this material.
An event during which people read books in order to raise money for charity.
ety: Blend of read + marathon; compare telethon, walkathon, etc.

senses: The festivities held after a wedding meal.
An after-hours drinking session in a public house.
After-school care service.
examples: To keep costs down at our wedding, we only had family at the banquet, but invited all our friends to the afters.
It was an afters pub, which meant it closed at 11 p.m., doors bolted, but with us all inside.

senses: One who polarizes; one who divides a group or community into two extremes.
A skid that results in a vehicle rotating such that its longitudinal axis is no longer aligned with its direction of linear motion.
The formation of a subsidiary company that continues the operations of part of the parent company; the company so formed.
examples: Sulayman al-Shulukhi, left, races his modified Subaru Impreza every weekend night and delights in describing wrecks and spinouts.

senses: A jet aircraft with some superior quality, such as large size or high speed.
examples: My souped-up superjet blew a gasket just as I was ready to take off, so I took it to a highly recommended repair shop known as "Mourdock's Murderous Mechanics".

senses: a type of vocal ornamentation; especially the variant used in the Near and Middle East
ety: Borrowed from Persian تحریر (tahrir), from Arabic تَحْرِير (taḥrīr, “liberation; release”).
examples: Karimi includes an extensive tahrir within the final syllable of the verse ...
But it should be emphasized that Iran and Azerbāijān, which partake of the same musical culture, have the most intricate and highly elaborate form of tahrir in the world.

senses: Resembling a chameleon: readily changing color or other attributes.
examples: But it's worth noting that, despite the dancers' skintight unitards (of a chameleonic fabric that picked up whatever color shone on it), the sexes are barely distinguishable.
David Johansen, the chameleonic and charismatic vocalist who fronted the New York Dolls and found solo success under the moniker Buster Poindexter, died on Friday, his publicist confirmed to NPR.

senses: A farmstead with its people, plants and animals, considered as a unit.
In the UK a college (or collectively its fellows) in Cambridge or Oxford.
ety: Borrowed from Latin domus. Doublet of dome and duomo.
examples: The domus was a unique and unprecedented concentration of tilled fields, seed and graain stores, people, and domestic animals, all coevolving with consequences no one could possibly have foreseen.

senses: To make universal, to make consistent or common across all cases.
To consider or depict as universal.
The wall of a pit
A type of accessory cloud, looking like shreds either attached to, or separated from, the main cloud formation; mainly associated with nimbostratus, cumulus, and cumulonimbus.
ety: Borrowed from Latin pannus (“cloth”). Doublet of pagne and pane.

senses: A dubia roach.
ety: Borrowed from Latin dubia, plural of dubium (literally “doubt”).

senses: To turn something to carbon, especially by heating it; to scorch or blacken.
A person who plays the trombone.
A person who studies cities and their growth.
An urban planner.
An engagement (promise to marry) between a man and a woman, made by themselves or by relatives.
ety: From Jewish Babylonian Aramaic קידושין (literally “sanctifications”), plural of קידוש. Syntactically equivalent to, but differs in meaning from, Hebrew קִדּוּשִׁים.
examples: Just as Kiddushin takes place when the groom puts a ring on his bride's finger, so we, too, wind a strap around our finger and are sanctified unto the Holy One, blessed be He.

senses: One of the cabalistic aspects of the soul, related to intellect and the awareness of God.
A rear foot.
ety: From Middle English hint fot; equivalent to hind + foot.

senses: Food that is intended to be eaten off the premises from which it is bought.
An establishment that prepares and sells food to be taken away on demand.
The capacity of a material to decompose over time as a result of biological activity, especially to be broken down by microorganisms.
A person who evades something.
During the Second World War, an Allied pilot shot down over enemy territory who then escaped back to his own side.
Any of many insects, of superfamily Fulgoroidea, that bear a remarkable resemblance to leaves and are capable of prodigious leaps.
examples: The sap-feeding planthoppers (Homoptera: Fulgoroidea) are ubiquitous in virtually all Hawaiian terrestrial ecosystems.
Planthoppers begin life as eggs deposited in fissures on the surface of their host plant or even beneath the bark.

senses: written in dialogue.
ety: From Ancient Greek διαλογικός (dialogikós, “related to a dialogue”), from διάλογος (diálogos, “conversation, discourse, dialogue”), equivalent to dialog + -ic.

senses: Like a nerd; having the traits of a nerd.
examples: The boys whose averageness is marked by their especially pale-skinned, scrawny, and nerdish appearances.

senses: An ulcer or fistula in the inner angle of the eye.
ety: From Latin aegilōps, from Ancient Greek αἰγίλωψ (aigílōps, “haver-grass (Aegilops neglecta)”).

senses: A pre-katana style Japanese sword, characterized by a longer blade with more curvature.
Equal distance.
examples: The men are ranged so as to form three sides of a square, and stand three deep, each prisoner being three yards from his fellow. This equidistance gives them the appearance of chess-men set out on a board.

senses: A short blow or gust.
A male haircut done with electric clippers.
ety: 1662, in sense “flutter as blown by wind”, as whiff + -le (“(frequentative)”) and (onomatopoeia) sound of wind, particularly a leaf fluttering in unsteady wind; compare whiff. Sense “something small or insignificant” is from 1680.

senses: Having a ringing or reverberating sound.
Having rings (circles), or a ring shape; annular.
A primitive, subconscious belieflike attitude which may contradict one's conscious beliefs.
ety: Apparently formed to contrast with belief, as if it were B-lief and this were A-lief.

senses: Straight-jawed.
ety: From ortho- (“straight, correct”) + -gnathic (suffix forming adjectives relating to the jaw), after New Latin orthognathus.

senses: One who collaborates, a collaborator.
The science that studies the blood serum, and especially the reaction between antigens and antibodies in serum.
Whose laminations have been removed.
ety: From de- + laminated, or from delaminate + -ed.

senses: Chlorogalum pomeridianum, soap plant, a California native plant used for soap
Sapindus saponaria, wingleaf soapberry
ety: From Mexican Spanish amole, from Classical Nahuatl ahmōlli.

senses: To sound loudly or harshly; to cry out, wail, lament.
To bleat, bellow, low.
ety: Origin obscure. Possibly from Middle English *blerten, from Old English *blǣrettan, a variant of Old English *blǣran (compare Middle English bleren, blaren, bloren (“to cry, bellow, wail”) > English blare, blore). Compare also Middle English blurden, English blurt.
